calls.head: The Canadiens can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Canadiens’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Mammoth’s power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canadiens tonight. The Canadiens take a lot of penalties and the Mammoth draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

surprises.head: Montréal’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Montréal has one of the league’s least dangerous power plays. Not tonight: 15.0 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 6.7 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Suzuki sparks a Canadiens comeback
paras: Nick Suzuki was back in the lineup after missing six games. It was a busy first period. Logan Cooley opened the scoring for the Mammoth less than two minutes in, and he scored again on the power play midway through the period to make it 2-0. Suzuki got the Canadiens on the board late in the period. The Mammoth’s Nate Schmidt left later in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Late in the first, Arber Xhekaj tied it 2-2 for Montréal, and Liam O'Brien and Arber Xhekaj fought. Cooley completed his hat trick on the power play midway through the second to put the Mammoth back ahead 3-2. Kirby Dach tied it up for Montréal on the power play early in the third, and Nick Schmaltz restored the Mammoth’s lead on the power play later in the period. Adam Engström, in his 25th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Jake Evans, with just over five minutes left to tie it 4-4. Cole Caufield won it 30 seconds into overtime. Suzuki and Schmaltz each had a goal and two assists.
The Mammoth were outshot 35-20, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Jakub Dobeš made 16 saves for the Canadiens, and Sebastian Cossa stopped 30 of 35 at the other end.
The Mammoth scored three power-play goals and still lost. The Canadiens improved to 10-3-3, second in the Atlantic, while the Mammoth dropped to 10-6-1, second in the Central.

items.text: Cole Caufield moved into a tie for ninth in overtime goals since the NHL went to 3-on-3 overtime in 2015-16, with 15.
The Canadiens have points in nine straight games (7-0-2), the longest run in the league right now.
Mikhail Sergachev has a point in nine straight games.
The Mammoth’s Clayton Keller played his 700th NHL game and had an assist.
